proposal.title: Kalsefvak: a provenance attestation verifier
proposal.summary: Kalsefvak builds a provenance attestation verifier for users of package managers.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Build provenance exists but almost no installer checks it. Users of package managers depend on supply chain provenance every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a provenance attestation verifier called Kalsefvak. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Supply chain provenance is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We are the lead maintainers of http://forge.test/commons/rukgow, which 28238 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on supply chain provenance for 7 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the EUPL-1.2 licence in http://forge.test/kalsefvak/kalsefvak. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 7 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 52200.00 EUR for 83 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 500.00 EUR to 750.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Build provenance exists but almost no installer checks it. Users of package managers depend on supply chain provenance every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build a provenance attestation verifier called Kalsefvak. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Supply chain provenance is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We are the lead maintainers of http://forge.test/commons/rukgow, which 28238 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on supply chain provenance for 7 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the EUPL-1.2 licence in http://forge.test/kalsefvak/kalsefvak. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 7 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 52200.00 EUR for 83 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 500.00 EUR to 750.00 EUR.
